name: The Backfire Awards
scope: The Backfire Awards site at backfireawards.com: the feed of nominee posts and Murphys, the carousels and their Instagram exports, The Midgley and The Murphy pages, the Categoric Table, search, the guidelines and terms, the Backfire Newsletter, and the merch.
colorNote: The Switchback palette from the logo, on every page: navy and cream grounds, orange for the one call to action, vermilion for oops, petrol and faded teal for links and data. No browns: warm hues are never mixed into dark grounds or used as faded washes. The 1970s scenes stay as illustration only. Type stays Big Shoulders Display, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono. Every color has a night value. The site look is still named 70s in code (html[data-look]) so saved choices keep working. Night dashboards use the seven chart colors in fixed order and a teal ramp for amounts; text on charts stays cream, color sits on marks only. Each of the ten patterns has its own color, listed in public/codebook-ui.js.
status: Approved by Erik 2026-10-20: the Switchback palette from the logo as the master palette, extended for data; 1970s scenes for illustration only

exemplar.headline: For outstanding achievement in unintended consequences
exemplar.body: The famous fixes that worked too well and created new problems, and the pattern behind each, for founders and inventors who want to see the next one coming.

rules.detail: The audience is founders and inventors: people who build fixes for a living. Choose examples a founder or inventor would recognize from their own work, and end on what the next builder can take from it. Plain words still apply. (Decided 2026-10-20; the positioning doc is in the Drive drafts folder.)
The joke is the award itself. The copy stays plain and factual and lets the facts carry the irony.
A nominee has to have worked. Say what problem it solved before saying what it caused.
State whether the harm was knowable, unforeseeable, partly knowable or still contested, and stick to documented effects.
Describe the decision and its effects. Leave out motives, character and private life, and nominate only public work.

rules.rule: Plain words for a general reader
rules.detail: Explain the chemistry or policy in a sentence a reader without the background can follow, as the Midgley page does.

rules.rule: Prose to argue, lists to scan
rules.detail: Argue a nomination in sentences. Criteria, moderation rules and fields go in lists.
Write year ranges as 1889 to 1944. Use commas, colons, periods or parentheses instead of em and en dashes.

gaps: There is no logo file for the full element mark: the masthead tile is drawn in HTML and CSS, and the only SVG is the favicon, which carries Mg alone.
The favicon sets Mg as live text in Arial Narrow, not Big Shoulders Display, and the text is not outlined, so it renders differently by platform.
The repository is named midgely-awards while the site, the package and the Pages project spell it Midgley.
The home page and Midgley page screenshots in images/ show the earlier classic look.
Avocado and muted rose are illustration colors; no text pairing has been measured for them.
